subject.title: [Bug]:  Isolated cron session agent loop continues consuming tokens after run marked "ok"

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: The direct fix PR and the competing open PR encode opposite product contracts, and the choice affects existing scheduled jobs, session-state retention, and upgrade recovery.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep the linked PR direction, add or explicitly scope an upgrade path for existing omitted jobs, and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only rejection
options.body: Continue through the strict-validation direction and close or rework the defaulting PR after documenting user recovery.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only default
options.body: Land only the new-job default and state that existing omitted jobs require operator action or a later migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep the linked PR direction, add or explicitly scope an upgrade path for existing omitted jobs, and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans cron store migration/default semantics and product compatibility, and recent history ties this account to the cron store boundary.
